title: Choose the visual world
question: Your blog documents experiments: what you tried, what broke, what you found. The roll landed on the research notebook. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Research Notebook
options.lineage: Bound quad-ruled laboratory notebooks, as kept by working researchers
options.thesis: Every post is a dated notebook entry: hypothesis, method, result, kept to the standard of a lab record.
materials: quad-ruled blue grid in the margins only
taped-in figure plates with caption strips
options.viewport: Index opens as the notebook's contents page: entry numbers, dates, and titles ruled on a grid, with the Cooties robot as the notebook's owner stamp.
options.risk: Tips into skeuomorphic costume if the grid reaches into the reading column.

options.label: Swiss Research Series
options.thesis: One modular grid disciplines every post, so four posts read as a deliberate series, not a sparse list.
options.case: Fuses well: categories become one signal color each and the grid carries rigor; loses some warmth and the hands-on voice.

options.label: Annotated Explainer
options.thesis: Marker annotations and draw-on arrows walk readers through your diagrams like a colleague at a whiteboard.
options.case: Fuses partly: great for your diagram-heavy posts, but reads less rigorous than the research-lab references you named.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: Sticky yellow sign bands orient readers through long posts section by section.
options.case: Fuses poorly because long-form reading has one path, so decision-point signage adds noise rather than orientation.

canonCard.label: Research-lab journal
canonCard.thesis: The Goodfire / Anthropic / Transformer Circuits standard, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A quiet masthead, then a dated list of posts with titles, one-line summaries, and figure thumbnails.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every lab blog; the author's hands-on voice has to carry distinctiveness.
